# d-SEAMS

> d-SEAMS reads molecular-dynamics trajectories and classifies ice with CHILL and CHILL+, topological cages, primitive rings, Steinhardt q_l, and ice and brine fronts. Use it from the command line, a language binding, or a supported simulation engine.

Each link below is the Markdown twin of a page on https://docs.dseams.info, served beside the HTML.

## Start

- [d-SEAMS](https://docs.dseams.info/index.md): d-SEAMS 2.14 reads a molecular-dynamics trajectory and names the ice in it.

## Getting started

- [Getting started](https://docs.dseams.info/getting-started/index.md): Install the engine, read one frame, and open the recording of that run.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.dseams.info/getting-started/quickstart.md): Install the engine, classify one cubic cell, then read one LAMMPS frame.
- [Install the engine](https://docs.dseams.info/getting-started/install.md): Release 2.14.0 provides the seams command, libyodaLib, libseams (include/seams.h), and libseams_lang (bindings/cxx/seams_lang.h).
- [Videos](https://docs.dseams.info/videos/index.md): Short screencasts of d-SEAMS in each language and tutorial are hosted on d-SEAMS on Odysee.

## User guide

- [User guide](https://docs.dseams.info/user/index.md): Recipes and worked examples, grouped by the job you came to do.
- [Classify ice](https://docs.dseams.info/user/classify.md): Name the ice in a frame with CHILL+, cages, or the symmetry classifier.
- [Classify ice on the mixed TIP4P example](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/bulk-ice.md): You classify one in-tree frame two ways: CHILL+ (a staggered or eclipsed star on each oxygen) and cage membership (hexagonal cage or double-diamond cage).
- [Ice and clathrate labels](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/ice-and-clathrate.md): You label one frame two ways. CHILL+ reads a staggered or eclipsed star.
- [Classify a clathrate](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/clathrate.md): Hexagonal cages on ice Ih, double-diamond cages on cubic ice, and the sI, sII and sH census on the repeated cells.
- [Classify a dump](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/classify-cli.md): You have a LAMMPS water dump and want counts.
- [CHILL+](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/chill-plus.md): Label every oxygen with the published CHILL+ rule, or with the OVITO rule.
- [The symmetry classifier](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/symmetry-classifier.md): Name the ice shell of each oxygen.
- [Rings, cages, and order](https://docs.dseams.info/user/order.md): Primitive rings, cage signatures, Steinhardt parameters, and the neighbour list they share.
- [Primitive rings](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/rings.md): The recording counts primitive rings on the mixed TIP4P frame, 511 rings, then the 256 six-rings of ice Ih.
- [Bond-orientational order parameters](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/order-parameters.md): The local Steinhardt parameter of atom i is
- [Primitive rings](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/rings.md): Count primitive rings on a frame you already have.
- [Cages and TRACE](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/cages-trace.md): Ask which molecules sit in a complete ice cage, or which polyhedra match a ring-size signature.
- [Local q4 and q6](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/q4-q6.md): Compute the local Steinhardt parameters on the cutoff shell.
- [Linkcell neighbours and carried updates](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/linkcell-carried.md): Build the cutoff neighbour list, then keep rings when only part of the next frame moved.
- [Cutoff neighbour lists](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/neighbour-lists.md): Build the cutoff list, choose the thread count, and read the pinned session that compared it with vesin, freud, matscipy, mdapy, and OVITO.
- [Choosing a cutoff and padding](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/cutoff-padding.md): The neighbour cutoff is the --cutoff of seams chill-plus.
- [Interfaces, nucleation, and brine](https://docs.dseams.info/user/interfaces.md): Ice fronts, a growing nucleus, and salt across the interface.
- [Ice-water interface](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/interface.md): The recording labels this basal frame with published CHILL+: hexagonal 352, water 434, and the stack HHHHHHHH....C.
- [Nucleation](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/nucleation.md): The recording reports mean q6-bar on the 148-frame mW trajectory.
- [Brine and NaCl](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/brine.md): The recording follows an ice front through a short brine run, then this 864-water frame with nine ions.
- [Basal profiles and the nucleation census](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/science-front.md): science-front reads a LAMMPS dump and writes either a basal layer profile or a single-trajectory nucleation census.
- [From a trajectory to the ice front](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/from-trajectory.md): You have a trajectory and want CHILL+ labels, the primitive rings, and the position of the ice front.
- [Ionic-liquid dumps](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/ionic-liquid.md): An ionic-liquid dump is a multi-type frame, and CHILL is the wrong score for the ions.
- [Confined ice](https://docs.dseams.info/user/confined.md): Ice in a nanotube or a monolayer, and a triclinic cell whose edge lengths are not the bound spans.
- [Confined water](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/confined-water.md): Quasi-one-dimensional ice is a stack of prism blocks.
- [Quasi-one-dimensional ice](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/nanotube.md): A nanotube ice is a stack of prism blocks of one ring size.
- [Confined ice](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/confined-ice.md): Classify ice in a nanotube or a monolayer.
- [Sheared cells](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/sheared-cells.md): You have a triclinic LAMMPS dump and want the engine to use the real cell, not a diagonal of bound spans.
- [Engines](https://docs.dseams.info/user/engines.md): Read a trajectory from LAMMPS, GROMACS, OpenMM, or PLUMED, or label the frame inside the run.
- [Run in situ](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/insitu-run.md): The recording scores the ice Ih cell: 128 hexagonal labels, 256 six-rings, and mean local q6 0.625855.
- [LAMMPS](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/engine-lammps.md): Build run_hook against conda-forge LAMMPS from 2024.8.29 up through the 2025 releases.
- [GROMACS](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/engine-gromacs.md): Build gmx-seams against conda-forge GROMACS 2026.3, or a later 2026 release.
- [OpenMM](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/engine-openmm.md): Build the reporter against conda-forge OpenMM 8.6.1 or a later 8 release.
- [PLUMED](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/engine-plumed.md): The thread count comes from PLUMED_NUM_THREADS.
- [In-situ CHILL+](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/engine-insitu.md): InSitu in adapters/python/dseams_insitu/engine.py classifies one frame during a run.
- [OpenMP target offload](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/openmp-offload.md): Build the Steinhardt kernel and the TUM ice score (hop-bound six-rings and cage affiliation) for an NVIDIA GPU.
- [Engine builds](https://docs.dseams.info/engines/index.md)
- [LAMMPS](https://docs.dseams.info/engines/lammps.md): Meson builds run_hook, the in-run hook.
- [GROMACS](https://docs.dseams.info/engines/gromacs.md): engines/gromacs/seams_ice.cpp is a TrajectoryAnalysisModule.
- [OpenMM](https://docs.dseams.info/engines/openmm.md): There is one reporter, DseamsReporter in adapters/python/dseams_insitu/openmm.py.
- [PLUMED](https://docs.dseams.info/engines/plumed.md): The thread count comes from PLUMED_NUM_THREADS.
- [In-situ](https://docs.dseams.info/engines/insitu.md): adapters/python/dseams_insitu/engine.py is InSitu.
- [Engine walkthroughs](https://docs.dseams.info/walkthrough/index.md): Each page analyzes a supplied input with published CHILL+, the primitive six-ring histogram, and local q6.
- [Language walkthroughs](https://docs.dseams.info/user/languages.md): The same ice cell from C, C++, and each binding, and from each engine driver.
- [C tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/c.md): Label the eight-atom cubic cell with seams.h and print the library version.
- [C++ tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/cpp.md): Classify the eight-atom cubic cell with include/seams.hpp, then the ice Ih dump.
- [Fortran](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/fortran.md): Classify ice Ih from Fortran. The recording uses input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj: seams read prints nop 128, and published CHILL+ at a 3.5 angstrom cutoff prints nop 128 hexagonal 128.
- [Julia](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/julia.md): Classify ice Ih from Julia. The recording uses input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj: seams read prints nop 128, and published CHILL+ at a 3.5 angstrom cutoff prints nop 128 hexagonal 128.
- [Lua and Fennel](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/lua.md): Classify a frame from Lua or Fennel. The recording follows require("dseams") and the same call from Fennel.
- [Python](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/python.md): Classify ice Ih from Python. The recording uses input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj: seams read prints nop 128, and published CHILL+ at a 3.5 angstrom cutoff prints nop 128 hexagonal 128.
- [R](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/r.md): Classify ice Ih from R. The recording uses input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj: seams read prints nop 128, and published CHILL+ at a 3.5 angstrom cutoff prints nop 128 hexagonal 128.
- [Rust](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/rust.md): Classify ice Ih from Rust. The recording uses input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj: seams read prints nop 128, and published CHILL+ at a 3.5 angstrom cutoff prints nop 128 hexagonal 128.
- [Engines tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/engines.md): Eight molecules of cubic ice are in engines/tutorial/ice.data.
- [GROMACS tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/gromacs.md): gmx-seams reads a trajectory after gmx mdrun and classifies it with seams_chill_plus.
- [In-situ tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/insitu.md): Eight cubic-ice atoms, one observation through InSitu.observe.
- [LAMMPS tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/lammps.md): engines/lammps/in.dseams is a frozen cubic cell of 64 atoms.
- [OpenMM tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/openmm.md): DseamsReporter in adapters/python/dseams_insitu/openmm.py asks for positions every interval and calls InSitu.observe.
- [PLUMED tutorial](https://docs.dseams.info/fronts/plumed.md): SEAMS reports three components on this page.
- [Paper figures](https://docs.dseams.info/user/paper.md): The in-tree numbers behind the published figures, and the gallery drawn from those runs.
- [Paper figures](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/paper-figures.md): The 2020 JCIM figures are drawn from figshare project 73545.
- [CHILL+ on an ice/water slab](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/paper-interface.md): An interface is where a rule is easy to fool.
- [Cage census of sI, sII and sH](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/paper-cages.md): A clathrate cage is a closed polyhedron of primitive rings.
- [Primitive rings and the shortest-path test](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/paper-rings.md): A ring search first walks every simple cycle up to a chosen size.
- [Ice growing into brine](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/paper-brine.md): The front is the height where the crystal slabs stop.
- [Ice-likeness along a short nucleation run](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/paper-nucleation.md): Ice-likeness here is the mean Lechner-Dellago \bar q_6.
- [Science gallery](https://docs.dseams.info/user/tutorials/gallery.md): These pictures show the interface, brine, ring, cage, and nucleation examples.
- [Science tutorials](https://docs.dseams.info/science/index.md): Three calculations from the papers, each using a small input: an ice-water interface, a brine freezing front, and clathrate cages.
- [Ice/liquid interface and nucleation](https://docs.dseams.info/science/interface.md): The interface dump is input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj, 864 waters in a cell 23 by 22 by 53 angstrom.
- [Brine freezing front](https://docs.dseams.info/science/brine.md): The d-SEAMS/brine-front-230K dataset provides the initial and final frames for a 20-pair loading.
- [sII and sH hydrate cages](https://docs.dseams.info/science/cages.md): input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj and input/traj/genice_sH.lammpstrj are guest-free GenIce hosts, 136 waters each.
- [Science figures](https://docs.dseams.info/science/gallery.md): These four molecular views accompany the science tutorials.
- [Performance and comparisons](https://docs.dseams.info/user/performance.md): What to time, how the literature codes were run, and where d-SEAMS sits next to them.
- [Benchmarks](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/benchmarks.md): Time a 2.14.0 build and write down the run.
- [Literature head-to-head](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/literature-h2h.md): Two recorded comparisons of d-SEAMS 2.14.0.
- [Reproduce the literature head-to-head](https://docs.dseams.info/user/howto/literature-reproduce.md): scripts/h2h_rc3_sitting.py writes the six-call sitting.
- [Head-to-head](https://docs.dseams.info/user/comparisons.md): Measured comparisons of d-SEAMS 2.14.0 with other structure codes.
- [Concepts](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/index.md): These pages are for understanding.
- [Architecture](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/architecture.md): 0 is one C++ engine, libyodaLib.
- [Binding overhead](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/binding-overhead.md): Ice Ih at 4096, 32768, and 110592 molecules.
- [The C API](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/c-api.md): include/seams.h is ABI 1 of libseams.
- [CHILL+: the published rule and the OVITO rule](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/chill-plus-rules.md): Nguyen and Molinero, /J. Phys. Chem. B/ 2015, 119, 9369 (10.1021/jp510289t), equation 1 averages q_3 over the four nearest neighbours of a shell that already holds four neighbours inside the cutoff.
- [CHILL+ versus cages](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/chill-plus-vs-cages.md): Two classifiers in the engine library libyodaLib answer different questions.
- [Citation](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/citation.md): If you use this software, cite the methods paper.
- [ClavisCage TRACE](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/clavis-trace.md): ClavisCage 0.3.18 runs TRACE (Hsu and Lin, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2025, 10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01459) on the same hydrate cells as d-SEAMS 2.14.0.
- [Carried rings and the hop ball](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/hop-ball.md): primitive::RingUpdater returns the primitive rings of one neighbour graph.
- [Interface and confined ice](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/interface-order.md): Two published CHILL+ rules, on the same coordinates, with the thresholds left alone.
- [Linkcell strong scaling](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/linkcell-scaling.md): An orthorhombic frame is cut across ranks by linkcell's weighted recursive coordinate bisection of the periodic cell grid.
- [Primitive rings and OVITO FindRings](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/ovito-findrings.md): A ring is primitive when every pair of its vertices is as close along the ring as it is through the rest of the graph.
- [Release-candidate sitting](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/performance.md): The tables are the release-candidate sitting of d-SEAMS 2.14.0.
- [Performance](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/performance-h2h.md): Head-to-head times for ice Ic and a TIP4P/ice liquid at 884736 molecules.
- [Performance overview](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/performance-overview.md): Each median is printed on one page.
- [Performance, 4096 to 110592](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/performance-range.md): Neighbour lists and primitive rings from the comparisons other than the release-candidate sitting and the 884736-molecule head-to-head.
- [Primitive rings and the full graph](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/primitive-rings.md): A ring is primitive when the graph distance between every pair of its vertices equals the shorter distance along the ring.
- [Ring-adjacent completion](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/ring-completion.md): ring::ringAdjacentCompletion fills a single vacancy on a labeled six-ring.
- [Rings on one thread](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/rings-one-thread.md): primitive::ringNetwork against OVITO 3.17.2 FindRingsModifier.
- [SQQ](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/sqq.md): SQQ 0.5.8 counts shortest-path chordless rings of size 4, 5 and 6.
- [Stacking disorder](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/stacking-disorder.md): Cubic ice and hexagonal ice are the same puckered hexagons stacked in two orders.
- [Local symmetry](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/symmetry.md): The classifier names each oxygen as ice Ih, ice Ic, stacking-disordered ice, or unmatched, and it can name a hydrate cage or a five- or six-ring when one cluster is passed in.
- [Topological network criteria](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/topological-network.md): These are the criteria the classifiers use.
- [TRACE and signature cages](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/trace-assembly.md): TRACE (Hsu and Lin, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2025, 10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01459) finds hydrate cages on a hydrogen-bond graph.
- [Signature-search thread controls](https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/trace-threads.md): The signature search reads one OpenMP width, and the neighbour list may narrow it.

## API reference

- [API reference](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/index.md): Lookup pages for the engine. Tutorials and how-tos live elsewhere.
- [Python Frame](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/python-frame.md): dseams.userframe.read in pydseamslib 2.14.0 returns a Frame over libseams_lang.
- [seams CLI](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/cli.md): The engine command is seams. The parser is Argum (the same parser as eonclient).
- [Data Formats](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/data-formats.md): seams and the C++ readers share one suffix table.
- [walk_compare](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/walk-compare.md): tests/walk_compare walks a LAMMPS dump and prints one row per frame.
- [API map](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/api.md): Lookup for the C++ identifiers in src/include/internal.
- [Nix flake](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/nix.md): The flake builds libyodaLib and the seams CLI with Meson. It does not build Python or Lua. There are no overlays.
- [One task on every front](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/cross-language.md): The task is CHILL+ on frame 1 of input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj, LAMMPS type 1.
- [Glossary](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/glossary.md)
- [2.14.0 release notes](https://docs.dseams.info/reference/release-2.14.md): These notes describe the user-visible changes since d-SEAMS 2.13.0.
- [C API](https://docs.dseams.info/capi/index.md): Every SEAMS_API function in include/seams.h.
- [C](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/c.md): seams.h is ABI 1 of libseams. A handle is opaque.
- [C++](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/cpp.md): include/seams.hpp is the header-only C++ API.
- [Python](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/python.md): pydseamslib provides import dseams and import pydseams.
- [Fortran](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/fortran.md): The Fortran binding is the fpm Git dependency dseams in d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran.
- [Julia](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/julia.md): Both live in d-SEAMS/Dseams.jl.
- [R](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/r.md): The R package dseams is d-SEAMS/dseams-r.
- [Lua and Fennel](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/lua.md): The Lua and Fennel library is d-SEAMS/yodaStruct.
- [Rust](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/rust.md): Both live in d-SEAMS/dseams-rs.
- [Command line](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/cli.md): seams reads a trajectory and prints one result.
- [Science front](https://docs.dseams.info/stable/science.md): src/include/internal/science_front.hpp is the C++ layer profile and the single-trajectory critical size.
- [Language APIs](https://docs.dseams.info/lang/index.md): seams-core documents the C API and the C++ front here.

## Project

- [Changelog](https://docs.dseams.info/development/changelog.md): Release notes for the d-SEAMS engine.

## Language bindings

- [PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib): Install the Python binding with pip install pydseamslib==2.14.0.
- [yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct): Clone the Lua and Fennel binding, then run luarocks make in the checkout.
- [dseams-r](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-r): Install the R binding with remotes::install_github("d-SEAMS/dseams-r").
- [Dseams.jl](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/Dseams.jl): Install the Julia binding with Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/d-SEAMS/Dseams.jl").
- [dseams-rs](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-rs): Install the Rust binding with cargo add dseams@2.14.0.
- [dseams-fortran](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran): Add the Fortran binding as an fpm Git dependency.
